description:
FILED s473w (Opus, 2026-09-09) from the #1502 CPAN-board census.  A BUNDLE by
population, not by mechanism: these are the board rows whose cause is a
Scalar::Util / Sub::Util / introspection primitive answering differently from
perl's, each with its own small mechanism, and none of them big enough to earn
a task on the day they were counted.  Split it when one is picked up.

Rows are from `baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv` (s473w).  Reproduce any of
them with `tools/run-dist-t.pl --no-dist-lib ~/.cpan/build/Scalar-List-Utils-1.70-0 t/<file>`
(the --no-dist-lib is oracle rule 2: the dist's unbuilt XS lib/ must not shadow
PCL's shim).

  refaddr.t     9 rows   refaddr identity over the box model â a COPY does not
                         keep the address (NS:Scalar copy does not preserve
                         reference/SV identity is the ruled half; these rows
                         are the measured consequence)
  reftype.t     4 rows   a REF-to-REF answers SCALAR where perl answers REF;
                         an IO handle answers undef where perl answers IO
  openhan.t     5 rows   openhandle(): a CLOSED bareword handle, an unopened
                         IO::Handle, an unopened IO::File and a plain string
                         are all misjudged
  getmagic-once.t 4 rows get-magic is fetched more than once per read (the
                         file counts FETCH calls on a tied scalar)
  weak.t        1 row    weaken/isweak â the box model has no weak references
  reductions.t  2 rows   DESTROY TIMING: intermediate temporaries are not
  sample.t      2 rows   destroyed at the point perl destroys them
  tainted.t     3 rows   TAINT is not modelled: Scalar::Util::tainted always
                         answers false (perl runs these under an interpreter
                         variable it considers tainted)

and three of the same flavour outside that dist:

  Class-Inspector class_inspector.t 1 row   ->subclasses walks the symbol table
                         and sees PCL's stash, not perl's
  Class-Inspector class_inspector__inc_to_local.t 1 row  %INC-to-path: "Found
                         ourself" â %INC holds the generated .lisp, not the .pm
  Try-Tiny named.t 3 rows + finally.t 1 row  a sub NAME read back through
                         Sub::Util::subname is the shim's ("Try::Tiny::try"),
                         not perl's "main::try {...} "

NOT ONE BUG.  Do not "fix #1571" â pick a line, probe it against perl, and
give it its own task if it is more than an afternoon.  The bundle exists so
the board's cause column can be complete without inventing eight tasks nobody
scheduled.


=== TWO MORE ROWS ARE THIS STUB (s490, Fable) ===
openhan.t rows 6 (`works with indirect filehandles`) and 8 (`works with in-memory files`) -- `is(openhandle($fh), undef)` after `close $fh` -- read FAILING on the 2026-09-18 board (got GLOB(0x..), expected undef) where the s473w snapshot had them passing.  lib/Scalar/Util.pm's `sub openhandle { $_[0] }` never answered undef for anything, so the earlier pass was on NOTHING (a closed lexical handle used to read as undef at that call).  Implementing openhandle (open handle / tied handle -> itself, else undef; perl's pure-perl fallback in older Scalar::Util::PP is the shape) fixes rows 4, 6, 8, 13, 15, 16, 20 together.  Re-bless owner: #1913.

=== s500a (Opus, 2026-09-30): the OPENHANDLE line is done ===
lib/Scalar/Util.pm's `sub openhandle { $_[0] }` stub is replaced by `builtin::openhandle($_[0])` -> runtime `p-openhandle`: the argument itself when it is a glob, a glob ref, a lexical handle or an IO/in-memory handle whose stream is OPEN (the same fact the implicit close of #2006(a) reads: a socket, or a stream whose target is open-stream-p), else undef.  perl never resolves a NAME here: openhandle("STDIN") / ("x") are undef, as are undef, a never-opened glob, a CLOSED lexical or bareword handle, a dirhandle and a non-glob ref (scratch/s500a/probes/oh.pl, 7 rows = perl 5.40.3; guard Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t "openhandle: open handles only").  The openhan.t rows (6, 8: closed indirect/in-memory handles) should now pass -- NOT re-measured on the board (no board leg in this batch).  Also in this batch: weaken/isweak (weak.t's row) -- the FLAG only, no refcount.
subject: CPAN-board bundle: the introspection primitives that answer differently from perl (refaddr identity, reftype REF/IO, openhandle, get-magic count, weaken, DESTROY timing, taint, %INC paths, subname) â 35 board rows, NOT one bug
